Simulate a nonignorably selected outcome with known truth

Source: R/simulate.R
simulate_shadow.Rd

Draws covariates, an outcome \(Y\) and an observation indicator \(R\) whose propensity depends on \(Y\), with the ratio of response propensities between outcome values bounded by \(e^{|\mathrm{tilt}|}\). Because the mechanism is known, the target, the observed-data law and the conditional observation rate \(r(x) = P(R = 1 \mid X = x)\) are returned exactly. The simulator exists so that examples and tests depend on no outside data.

Usage

simulate_shadow(
  n = 5000,
  tilt = -1,
  outcome = c("binary", "continuous"),
  seed = 1L
)

obs_quantiles(sim, K = 200L)

Arguments

n

Number of rows.

tilt

The log of the largest ratio \(b\) of response propensities. Negative values mean that a high outcome (a default, \(Y = 1\), or a large loss) lowers the chance of being observed, as when such cases are more likely to have been rejected. 0 is ignorable selection.

outcome

"binary" (default) or "continuous".

seed

Seed for the random number generator. The caller's RNG state is restored on exit.

sim

A data frame from simulate_shadow(outcome = "continuous").

K

Number of quantile levels, \((k - 1/2)/K\).

Value

A data frame with columns x1, x2, z_shadow, z_policy, z_score, y (the outcome, NA where unobserved), observed (0/1) and the exact truth columns described above. Attributes "tilt" and "outcome".

obs_quantiles(): the exact \(n \times K\) matrix of conditional quantiles of \(Y\) given \(R = 1, X = x_i\).

Details

The covariates play fixed roles, so that shadow_screen() has something to find:

  • x1, x2: ordinary covariates entering both outcome and selection.

  • z_shadow: enters the outcome only, a valid shadow variable.

  • z_policy: enters the selection only, high exclusion violation and no relevance.

  • z_score: enters both strongly, like a bureau score that is also used in the acceptance decision.

Linear index of the outcome: \(\mu = 0.8 x_1 - 0.5 x_2 + 0.6 z_{\mathrm{shadow}} + 1.0 z_{\mathrm{score}}\); of selection: \(g = 0.8 - 0.8 x_1 + 0.4 x_2 + 1.0 z_{\mathrm{policy}} - 1.0 z_{\mathrm{score}}\). All truth columns condition on all five covariates.

Binary (outcome = "binary"): \(\eta = \mathrm{expit}(\mu - 1.5)\), \(\pi(0,x) = \mathrm{expit}(g)\min(1, e^{-b})\) and \(\pi(1,x) = \pi(0,x)e^{b}\) with \(b\) = tilt. Truth: eta, eta_obs, obs_rate.

Continuous (outcome = "continuous"): \(Y = \mu + \varepsilon\), \(\varepsilon \sim N(0,1)\), and \(\pi(y,x) = c(x)\exp\{b\, \Phi(\varepsilon)\}\) with \(c(x) = \mathrm{expit}(g)\min(1, e^{-b})\). Since \(\Phi(\varepsilon)\) is uniform, the ratio of propensities is at most \(e^{|b|}\), \(r(x) = c(x)(e^{b} - 1)/b\), and the quantile function of \(Y\) given \(R = 1, X = x\) is \(\mu(x) + \Phi^{-1}[\log\{1 + p(e^{b} - 1)\}/b]\), all in closed form. Truth: mu \(= E(Y \mid x)\), mean_obs \(= E(Y \mid R = 1, x)\), obs_rate; obs_quantiles() returns the quantile grid that sharp_scan_mean() takes.

Examples

d <- simulate_shadow(2000, tilt = -1, seed = 1)
head(d)
#>           x1          x2   z_shadow    z_policy    z_score  y observed
#> 1 -0.6264538 -0.88614959 -1.1346302 -0.61882708  0.2637034  0        1
#> 2  0.1836433 -1.92225490  0.7645571 -1.10942196 -0.8294518 NA        0
#> 3 -0.8356286  1.61970074  0.5707101 -2.17033523 -1.4616348 NA        0
#> 4  1.5952808  0.51926990 -1.3516939 -0.03130307  1.6839902 NA        0
#> 5  0.3295078 -0.05584993 -2.0298855 -0.26039848 -1.5443243 NA        0
#> 6 -0.8204684  0.69641761  0.5904787  0.53443047 -0.1908871  0        1
#>          eta     eta_obs   obs_rate
#> 1 0.12183541 0.048560624 0.47629521
#> 2 0.31806567 0.146455571 0.32143524
#> 3 0.01634164 0.006074504 0.79510116
#> 4 0.59617762 0.351959635 0.07534637
#> 5 0.01851066 0.006890315 0.84786452
#> 6 0.08776912 0.034185063 0.87019366
dc <- simulate_shadow(2000, tilt = -1, outcome = "continuous", seed = 1)
head(dc)
#>           x1          x2   z_shadow    z_policy    z_score         y observed
#> 1 -0.6264538 -0.88614959 -1.1346302 -0.61882708  0.2637034        NA        0
#> 2  0.1836433 -1.92225490  0.7645571 -1.10942196 -0.8294518        NA        0
#> 3 -0.8356286  1.61970074  0.5707101 -2.17033523 -1.4616348        NA        0

#> 5  0.3295078 -0.05584993 -2.0298855 -0.26039848 -1.5443243        NA        0
#> 6 -0.8204684  0.69641761  0.5904787  0.53443047 -0.1908871 -1.366172        1
#>           mu   mean_obs   obs_rate
#> 1 -0.4751630 -0.7532270 0.32619803
